metadata.title: Six Levels
metadata.purpose: Walk viewers through six progressive levels of Claude mastery — from the AskUserQuestion trick to Claude Code — so they can locate themselves and take one concrete next step.
metadata.clock: narration (Kokoro) — durations are word-count estimates until GATE 0 audio lock

beats.narration_text: Zdravo. this is Liam, in for Bear. being good at AI is stupidly simple. six levels. you are probably already on one of them. here is where to go next.

props.ask: how do I actually get good at using Claude?
props.answer_preview: start with AskUserQuestion — it makes Claude ask you the questions instead of...
props.command: Zdravo. this is Liam, in for Bear. being good at AI is…

beats.narration_text: level 1. the trick is AskUserQuestion. instead of you prompting Claude badly, Claude asks you the questions. prompt it like this: help me do X. use AskUserQuestion first. Claude gives you three to five questions. you click the answers. the more you say, the better the output. that one line makes you better at AI than most people who call themselves prompt engineers.

card.sub: AskUserQuestion — Claude interviews you, then builds

beats.narration_text: level 2. talk to your computer. you type four times slower than you talk. use a voice input tool — Wispr Flow has a free tier — and just speak. the AI transcribes, formats, sends. typing is 2024. speaking is now. level 3. download the Claude desktop app. open the Cowork tab. make a folder on your computer called cowork. drag it into Cowork. Claude can now read every file inside it.

card.sub: Wispr Flow free tier — voice input straight to Claude

beats.narration_text: level 3. Claude Cowork is different from the browser. the browser gives you text to copy. Cowork makes the actual file — the real PDF, the real spreadsheet — and saves it in your folder. drop in a messy doc, an old proposal, last month's numbers. now prompt it: build a spreadsheet to do X. ask me what you need first. three minutes later, a clean Excel file. in your folder.

card.sub: Cowork saves actual files — not text to copy-paste

beats.narration_text: level 4. connect your apps. left sidebar in the desktop app — click customize, then connectors. connect Gmail. connect Calendar. connect your meeting notes app. now Claude has context. you can prompt things like: what meetings do I have tomorrow and what prep do I need? AI just needs context. it needs to know you.

level 5. teach Claude new skills. go to the left sidebar, find customize, find skills. Claude already has a skill to create skills — it is called /skill-creator. just say what you need: I want to teach Claude how to make Excel spreadsheets the way I love them. add: but ask me questions first. you answer. Claude builds the skill. you can share it with your team.

card.sub: Claude teaches itself new skills — you just describe what you need

beats.narration_text: final boss. Claude Code. in the app, open the code tab — the angle-bracket icon in the left sidebar. turn on bypass permissions — all that means is: go, I trust you. then same trick: build a page where people book a call with me. ask me questions first. Claude asks about dark mode, calendar integration, confirmation emails. you click. four minutes later — it works. you did not write a single line of code.

beats.narration_text: pick the level you are on right now. do just the next one. open Claude. start at level 1. tonight.

card.sub: Open Claude and start at whichever level is one above where you are now

beats.narration_text: six levels. you do not need all six today. most people never try even level 1. the bar to knowing is just trying. this is Liam, in for Bear.

card.sub: this is Liam, in for Bear

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this: you want to understand what it actually means to get good at Claude — beyond just writing better prompts. Ask Claude to walk you through the six levels of Claude proficiency: what changes at each level, which level is the most common plateau, and what the jump from level three to level four actually requires.
